stack.our_stance: NO LONGER LIGHT. Neocloud was cut to ~5% in the 2026-07-17 RV reset after the froth de-rated 30-40%, but the spender exclusion came off on 2026-08-03 and GOOGL (4.5% of notional) and AMZN (3.9%) entered the book. stack.label: Models
stack.our_stance: NO DIRECT POSITION, BARRED NOT ABSENT. The instruments exist: Binance lists ANTHROPIC and OPENAI as PREMARKET perps and this book held ANTHROPIC until 2026-07-27. Policy 1.3 / Part 4 bars pre-IPO instruments from the quant sleeve, which is why the weight is zero. Direct weight is not the same as exposure: Alphabet consolidates DeepMind and Gemini and Amazon carries the Anthropic stake plus Trainium and Bedrock, so at 8.4% of notional the book already owns frontier-lab economics inside two listed names. SpaceX is the weaker case, an equity stake in xAI rather than a lab it operates.

entries.author: Chamath Palihapitiya
entries.title: AI investing guide, by layer
entries.claim: Ranks the AI stack by expected cash-on-cash return. Land and power is the fastest path and energized land can explode in value as data centres face pushback; has acquired ~6GW coming online 2026-2029. Will not invest in silicon startups: performance demands, manufacturing precision and memory supply-chain access now foreclose new entrants. Clouds are lucrative but risk:reward is skewed by coming KYC and alignment obligations. Models are an open question because revenue may be inflated by tokenmaxxing. Harnesses and applications are where the durable value accrues.

layer_views.note: about STARTUPS competing with Nvidia, NOT a short on listed semis

entries.vs_our_book: MIXED. He is most bullish precisely where we are lightest (power/grid), which corroborates our own layer-mix flag. His silicon caution is a venture-entry argument, not a short on listed semis, so it does NOT contradict our semi-heavy book. His two highest-conviction layers are ones we cannot access.

entries.author: Gavin Baker
entries.title: Hyperscaler credit spreads are being misread
entries.claim: The selloff prices widening hyperscaler credit spreads as a solvency signal, but spot GPU rental prices run at least 2x contracted rates, so hyperscalers are currently UNDER-earning and will reprice higher as contracts roll off. Models hyperscaler operating cash flow growth accelerating from 31% in Q1 2026 to 50% in Q2, an acceleration absent from estimates that wrongly model a Q3 deceleration. At ~$60B per gigawatt, 25-35GW of CY28 capex implies $1.5-2.2T against $1.3-1.4T of consensus operating cash flow, and he expects that gap to close on upward revisions rather than debt. Notes CDS markets are easily manipulated (short the stock, buy the CDS) so he attaches little signal to them. Names power delivery, not funding, as the real risk.

questions the BofA framing of FCF transferring to semis

entries.vs_our_book: WE TOOK PART OF THIS BET. Written on 2026-08-01 against a universe that still barred hyperscalers; the exclusion came off two days later, on measurement rather than on his argument, and GOOGL and AMZN are now held at 4.5% and 3.9% of notional. So this is no longer a challenge to a screen we run, it is the bull case for names we own, and what is exposed is our SIZE rather than our exclusion. Still live as a test: if hyperscaler OCF does accelerate toward 50%, the book is under-weight the trade, which is the opposite of the risk this entry used to describe. His power-delivery caveat lands on our lightest layer (power/grid, 5.0% of notional) and is the sharper warning of the two.

entries.author: Coatue
entries.title: The market is rewarding the sellers of the shortage
entries.claim: Splits the AI complex into sellers of the shortage (semis, memory, optics: pricing power, fixed cost base, large upward EPS revisions) and buyers of the shortage (hyperscaler capex, modest revisions). Sellers +107% YTD against buyers +4%.

layer_views.note: the buyers; excluded from our universe

entries.vs_our_book: ORIGIN OF THE FRAMING, NOT LIVE EVIDENCE. The supplier/spender split still describes how the thesis leg ranks names, and the long book is still supplier-heavy. But the tradeable version of this claim was TESTED AND REFUTED on 2026-08-03 (claims_register: coatue_sellers_vs_buyers): excluding the spenders scored 3.62 vs 3.56 for the full universe, inside noise, with the entire edge in the oldest sub-period and gone in the two most recent. It is backward-looking price evidence, and it justified barring six names for seven weeks. Cite it for where the framing came from; do not cite it as validation of a screen we no longer run.

thesis: Trackable AI-frontier smart money — crossover funds that backed the private SpaceX / OpenAI / Anthropic rounds AND file 13F-HR, so their public books reveal their picks-and-shovels bets. Full books (not just our overlap) future-proof us: as Binance lists more tokenized stocks, we already know who backs each name.
